newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arab police to meet in Algeria on "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Arab police to meet in Algeria on "terrorism".

text.p: Officials in charge of security forces and police in 21 Arab countries are to meet in Algeria next week to draw on its experience in fighting "terrorism", Algeria's term for armed Moslem fundamentalists.

The official Algerian news APS said on Friday the 20th congress of Arab police and security services would be held from October 14 to 16 "to look at the need to reinforce cooperation between Arab countries against this plague".
A spokesman for Algerian security services was quoted as saying: "Algeria's experience in fighting terrorism makes it a model for Arab countries which realise that criminality has no frontiers."
APS said the meeting, attended by 21 Arab countries which are members of the Council of Arab Interior Ministers, would hear evidence of improvement in Algeria's security situation.
Algerian security forces and Moslem guerrillas have been locked in conflict since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election which Islamists were poised to win.
An estimated 50,000 people have been killed since then.

Earlier this week, Moslem guerrillas killed 34 people in an ambush in southern Algeria and shot dead a woman school teacher and wounded five other people in the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital Algiers.
